To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the space requirements for finishing feeders in a 1:1 ratio of feeders to pigs are 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 m2 per feeder for 21, 32, and 45 kg pigs, respectively.
the number of pigs per feeder is not a reliable predictor of feeder space requirement, and the space requirements of a feeder are not constant over time
the space requirements for feeder capacity are 0.5, 0.8, and 1.0 square foot per head, respectively, for 21-, 31-, and 45-kg finishing swine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the determination of the optimum space requirements of finishing swine feeders.
the development of an efficient method of determining the space requirement of a feeder.
the evaluation of space requirements for finishing swine feeders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a feeder space requirement of 0.25 to 0.30 square feet per head for finishing pigs is appropriate.
the feeder capacity of the 21, 28, 31, 36 and 45 finishing pigs was 1.2 kg, 1.8 kg, 3.2 kg, and 5.0 kg of corn per day.
45 pigs per feeder is the most efficient and practical space requirement for finishing feeders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feeder space requirements for growing and finishing swine are highly influenced by feeder design, feeder placement, and feeder management.
feeder space requirements for finishing swine can be evaluated using time-lapse video.
feeder space requirements are not a function of feeder size or design, and that feeder space requirements for finishing pigs are not a function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
swine finishers are capable of eating more food than is currently provided in commercial feeders, but the rate at which they eat is not as fast as previously believed.
swine finishing feeders should not be designed for a specific number of swine.

we can use the time-lapse videos to determine how many swine can be fed in a given space, and that the feeder capacity is dependent on the size of the feeder, number of swine, and amount of feed in the feeder.
